verdict.reasoning: Chief complaint of dysuria is supported by: Patient: "It hurts when I pee."
Duration of 6 days is stated: Doctor: "how long has that been going on for?" Patient: "Uh, six days."
Foul-smelling urine is described: Patient: "I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out."
Intermittent midline suprapubic pain rated 7/10 is supported: Patient: "I've got, pain in my tummy." "In my lower tummy." "In the middle." Pain score: "Seven... Seven." and "Comes and goes."
Visible blood spots in urine are described: Patient: "I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine. Spots."

Denials are present: Fever: Patient: "No, not at all." Back/loin pain: Doctor: "any... lower back pain?... no loin pain as well." Patient does not report any; vaginal discharge: Doctor: "any vaginal discharge or, anything like that?" Patient: "No, just the blood spot..." This supports denial of fever, flank/loin pain, back pain, and vaginal discharge.
Eating and drinking okay is stated: Doctor: "have you been able to eat and drink OK?" Patient: "Yes."
History of IBS is recorded: Patient: "I had IBS before."

Mebeverine regimen is specified: Doctor: "Do you take that regularly?" Patient: "Yes." Doctor: "And it, do you take it three times a day?" Patient: "Yes I do." Doctor: "Two hundred milligrams?" Patient: "Yes."
Allergy documented: Doctor: "Any allergies?" Patient: "Clindamycin." Doctor: "You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK."
Living situation is stated: Doctor: "whereabouts, do you live? Do you live with friends, family?" Patient: "I live with friends."
Occupation is stated: Doctor: "where do you work? What's your job?" Patient: "I'm a support worker."
Alcohol and smoking history are described: Patient: "Occasionally." then "One glass of wine a week." and Doctor: "And do you smoke?" Patient: "No."
Regular menses documented: Doctor: "Do you have regular periods?" Patient: "Yes I do."

Clinician impression of a lower UTI with hematuria is consistent: Doctor: "it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine." Presence of dysuria and "spotted, uh, blood in my urine" supports lower urinary tract infection with hematuria; no systemic or flank symptoms suggests uncomplicated lower UTI.
Empiric 3‑day antibiotics are prescribed: Doctor: "we can treat this infection... with a course of antibiotics." and "It would just be for three days." plus prescription to pharmacy.
Hydration advice: Doctor: "drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day."

OTC cranberry and sachets advised: Doctor: "you can get some cranberry juice and take, drink that as well... And also some, sachets... from the chemist, some sachets which just help change the acidity of your urine."

Safety‑net advice given: Doctor: "if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling, you get lower back pain, um, or you're getting a high temperature, or you have any problems actually passing urine. Then it's very important that we speak to you again." and also if symptoms not resolving or recurrent.

Thermometer and home monitoring advised: Doctor: "Have you got a thermometer at home?" Patient: "No." Doctor: "It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature, just to make sure that it isn't, going up and down."
